title: Capability runway and sprint hedging for Private instances
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: define a capability-by-sprint runway and an explicit sprint hedging policy for Private/VPC/on-prem releases so that we can deliver SLA-sensitive features with predictable risk and capacity profiles.

Scope: RBAC v1 (role templates + audit trails), KMS/HSM integration for tenant keys, automated in-place private upgrade tooling (0-downtime paths and rollback), expanded telemetry retention for offline evals, and tenant compatibility matrix checks. This ticket is the PM playbook + acceptance criteria + tranche mapping that other squads will consume.

Why: customers adopting Private instances have variable infra (air-gapped, restrictive egress, custom KMS). Historical failures on previous upgrades and misaligned expectations caused two incidents last year. We need a documented cadence that balances momentum with hedge capacity to reduce regressions and unexpected rollbacks.

Key deliverables: capability runway doc (feature -> tranche mapping), sprint hedging guidelines (buffer allocation per sprint, emergency buffer process), rollout gating criteria (compatibility check pass, telemetry health signals), cross-team runbook for upgrade rollback, and a CANARY policy that sequences Dedicated -> Private minimal tenants -> broad rollout.

Success metrics: no more than 1 customer-impacting rollback per quarter for private upgrades; upgrade success rate >= 98% on first attempt in canary tenants; mean time to rollout decision < 4 hours when a compatibility flag fires.

Acceptance criteria and signoffs are enumerated below and must be met before beginning tranche 2 rollouts.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff sync with Eng (runtime, infra) and Security. Agreed tranche taxonomy: TR1 (compatibility fixes + RBAC v1), TR2 (KMS/HSM + telemetry retention), TR3 (upgrade automation + tenant tooling). Action: ENG to provide risk estimate per feature by 2025-02-19. (Owner: Ravi)

2025-02-19: Engineering risk estimates received. Runtime team flagged KV-cache schema migration as high-risk for in-place upgrades. Decided to move KV migration to a dark-launch approach in TR3 and add migration feature flag. Added 2 buffer points to sprint hedging for TR3. (Owner: Miguel Santos)

2025-02-26: Design and Docs draft created for customer-facing upgrade expectations. Reviewed by Solutions Eng; wording updated to include explicit rollback windows and contact path. PRD link added to artifacts. (Owner: Aisha)

2025-03-03: Security review kickoff. Initial KMS threat model OK but HSM hardware attestation flows require additional spec from Infra team. Security requested a staging KMS connector test matrix. (Owner: Elena Martinez)

2025-03-05: PM review with Director: approved runway approach pending two changes: (1) add measurable telemetry health thresholds to gating criteria; (2) formalize post-rollout incident learning checklist. Incorporated into acceptance_criteria. Planning follow-up cross-team rehearsal on 2025-03-20.
acceptance_criteria: Tranche mapping published with owners for each feature (doc + Confluence link added to artifacts).
Compatibility matrix tool (automated checks) runs against 90% of targeted customer images in canary and passes smoke tests for TR1 features.
Telemetry health thresholds defined and hooked into Console dashboards (token-level latency, 99th ms, error-rate by tenant).
Upgrade runbook completed with rollback playbook and test checklist; rehearse runbook in DR environment with at least 2 dry runs.
Security signoff for KMS flows and a staging HSM test plan documented.
Sprint hedging policy adopted by squads: 10-20% buffer of sprint velocity reserved for unplanned compatibility work; emergency escalation path documented.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive tranches speed time-to-value but increase cross-customer risk; hedge by using a conservative TR1 then faster TR2/3 if signals are green.
Decision: prefer feature flags and dark-launch migration for schema changes to avoid tenant-wide disruptions.
Stakeholder feedback: Solutions Eng recommends a customer communication template for upgrade windows; Sales requests a 'managed-upgrade' flag for high-touch customers (follow-up ticket).
Risk: customers with strict air-gap policies may require manual KMS binding; include professional services estimate in customer contract workstreams.
